user.title: Connect to AlphaESS Portal
user.description: Sign in with your current AlphaESS customer portal account. The wallbox serial number is optional and can be added later through Reconfigure if it is not detected automatically.

data_description.username: Username or email address for the AlphaESS portal (cloud.alphaess.com).
data_description.password: Password for your AlphaESS portal account.
data_description.system_serial: Serial number of your storage system (e.g. AL... on the nameplate).
data_description.wallbox_serial: Serial number of the wallbox (starts with ALP...). Leave empty for auto-detection.

reconfigure.title: Assign wallbox
reconfigure.description: Enter the wallbox serial number. It starts with ALP.

data_description.wallbox_serial: Serial number of the wallbox (starts with ALP...).

init.title: Options
init.description:
Select an area to configure:
• Refresh interval and monitoring sensors for PV analysis
• PV charging control (mode 5): thresholds, wait times and protection rules
• Vehicle profiles: measured charging power curves

general.title: Refresh interval and monitoring sensors
general.description: Whole seconds from 5 to 300 are allowed. Short intervals cause correspondingly frequent cloud requests and may be rate limited. Defaults: G1T 120 seconds, G2T 30 seconds. Select the local sensors for future PV charging analysis. The wallbox power sensor is provided by this integration and does not need selection.

data.battery_soc_entity: Home battery state of charge sensor

data_description.update_interval_seconds: Polling interval for the AlphaESS cloud portal in seconds (5–300 s). Example: 30 s for G2T wallboxes for prompt status updates; 120 s for G1T to prevent portal throttling.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Sensor for current photovoltaic generation in W or kW. Positive when generating. Example: sensor.solar_power or sensor.pv_power (e.g. 4500 W).
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Sensor for current home battery state of charge in percent. Example: sensor.battery_soc or sensor.home_battery_soc (e.g. 75%).
data_description.household_power_entity: Sensor for total household load including the wallbox in W or kW. Example: sensor.house_load or sensor.household_power (e.g. 800 W idle or 4940 W while charging).
data_description.grid_power_entity: Sensor for grid power at the meter in W or kW. Positive = grid import, negative = grid export. Example: sensor.grid_power (e.g. +250 W import or -3200 W export).
data_description.battery_power_entity: Optional sensor for home battery charge/discharge power in W or kW. Positive = discharging, negative = charging. Example: sensor.battery_power (e.g. +1500 W discharge).

control.title: PV charging control (mode 5)
control.description: Settings for HA charging mode 5, activated via the charging mode select option "PV-Eigenverbrauch". Defaults are based on the measurement cycle of 2026-10-13; power limits and battery values are provisional proposals.

data.grid_import_limit_w: Grid import protection: tolerance above permitted deficit

data_description.active_vehicle_profile: Vehicle profile with the charging stages (phases, current, measured power) the controller chooses from. Example: Standard vehicle (single-phase 6–16 A from 1.38 kW, three-phase 6–16 A from 4.14 kW).
data_description.control_strategy: Step control changes exactly one stage per decision (calmer, gentler); direct control jumps straight to the highest matching stage (faster PV utilization). Applies to increasing and decreasing. Example: When surplus jumps from 1.5 kW to 5 kW, step control shifts from 6 A to 7 A, whereas direct control jumps straight to three-phase 7 A.
data_description.average_window_seconds: PV, house load and grid import are averaged over this moving window before a regular decision is made. Applies to increasing and decreasing. Longer = calmer but slower. Example: 120 s smooths over passing clouds or a coffee machine (2000 W for 1 minute) without immediately throttling charging.
data_description.unstable_average_window_seconds: Used while a stage marked unstable is active, so that power oscillation does not trigger further stage changes. Applies to increasing and decreasing. Example: 240 s on single-phase 6 A if the car's onboard charger periodically oscillates by 200 W at minimum current.
data_description.current_change_wait_seconds: Pause after a current change or a failed command before averaging restarts. Measured: the wallbox reacts about 25–29 s after the command. Applies in both directions. Example: 60 s gives the wallbox and vehicle 30 s reaction time plus 30 s to settle.
data_description.phase_change_wait_seconds: Pause after a phase change or a switch to/from mode 1. Measured: charging pauses about 35–45 s after the command for 10–15 s. Applies in both directions. Example: 90 s safely bridges the 15-second charging pause during relay switching between 1- and 3-phase.
data_description.allowed_grid_import_w: Power by which charging may permanently exceed the PV surplus; covered by the home battery or the grid. The controller works with surplus + this value when starting, increasing and decreasing. 0 = PV surplus only. Example: 1000 W allows charging at 2.4 kW (single-phase 10 A) with only 1.4 kW PV surplus. Can also be adjusted live via the 'Permitted Deficit' slider.
data_description.grid_import_limit_w: Decreasing only: grid import protection triggers when the average grid import exceeds the permitted deficit by more than this amount. Higher = more grid import is tolerated before reducing. Example: With 500 W permitted deficit and 200 W tolerance, protection only triggers above 700 W actual grid import.
data_description.grid_import_protection_seconds: Decreasing only: if the average grid import stays above the limit for this long, power is reduced immediately without waiting for the full averaging window. Longer = slower. Example: 30 s reduces power after 30 s instead of waiting 120 s when a stove or oven (e.g. 3000 W) is turned on.
data_description.reaction_confirm_seconds: If the house load stays within the range of the expected new load for this long after a command, the wait ends early. If other consumers change the load, the full wait applies. 0 = off. Example: 10 s ends the 60 s pause after about 35 s once the car has visibly settled on the new stage after 25 s.
data_description.surplus_reserve_w: Increasing only: increase only if the average surplus exceeds the power of the next stage by at least this amount. Higher = less oscillation and grid import, but more feed-in. Example: 200 W reserve: Next stage requires 4140 W -> step up only once budget reaches 4340 W.
data_description.min_battery_soc: Below this home battery state of charge the controller switches the wallbox to mode 1 (the wallbox's own surplus charging) to protect the battery. Example: 30% preserves the home battery for evening and night household base load.
data_description.battery_soc_hysteresis: After SOC protection, control resumes only once the home battery exceeds the minimum SOC by this amount. Prevents rapid on/off toggling. Example: 10% hysteresis with 30% minimum SOC means control resumes only at 40% SOC.
data_description.sensor_stale_seconds: If a sensor delivers no new value for this long, the measurement is invalid and the wallbox is switched to mode 1 as a fallback. Example: 30 s quickly detects a failed smart meter or Wi-Fi disconnection.
data_description.sensor_recovery_seconds: All sensors must deliver valid values continuously for this long before control resumes after a sensor outage. Example: 60 s ensures readings have stabilized after a sensor restart.

vehicles.title: Vehicle profiles
vehicles.description: Manage vehicle profiles: add new vehicles, edit existing profiles or delete unused ones.

vehicle_add.title: Add vehicle
vehicle_add.description: Enter the stable charging power after settling for each phase/current combination. Unstable stages are used with a longer averaging period; excluded stages are never selected.

power_1p.name: Single-phase charging power
power_1p.description: Measured stable charging power in watts for single-phase charging (e.g. 6 A ≈ 1380 W, 10 A ≈ 2300 W, 16 A ≈ 3680 W).

power_3p.name: Three-phase charging power
power_3p.description: Measured stable charging power in watts for three-phase charging (e.g. 6 A ≈ 4140 W, 10 A ≈ 6900 W, 16 A ≈ 11040 W).

data_description.name: Vehicle name for identification in the selection dialog. Example: Tesla Model 3, Renault Zoe, ID.4 or Standard vehicle.
data_description.unstable_stages: Charging stages where this vehicle oscillates or charging power fluctuates. The longer averaging window applies to these stages. Example: single-phase 6 A if the onboard charger is unstable at minimum current.
data_description.excluded_stages: Charging stages the controller must never select for this vehicle. Example: single-phase 16 A (if the charging cable is limited to 15 A) or three-phase 6 A (if 3-phase charging should only start at 8 A).

vehicle_edit.title: Edit vehicle
vehicle_edit.description: Enter the stable charging power after settling for each phase/current combination. Unstable stages are used with a longer averaging period; excluded stages are never selected.

power_1p.name: Single-phase charging power
power_1p.description: Measured stable charging power in watts for single-phase charging (e.g. 6 A ≈ 1380 W, 10 A ≈ 2300 W, 16 A ≈ 3680 W).

power_3p.name: Three-phase charging power
power_3p.description: Measured stable charging power in watts for three-phase charging (e.g. 6 A ≈ 4140 W, 10 A ≈ 6900 W, 16 A ≈ 11040 W).

data_description.name: Vehicle name for identification in the selection dialog. Example: Tesla Model 3, Renault Zoe, ID.4 or Standard vehicle.
data_description.unstable_stages: Charging stages where this vehicle oscillates or charging power fluctuates. The longer averaging window applies to these stages. Example: single-phase 6 A if the onboard charger is unstable at minimum current.
data_description.excluded_stages: Charging stages the controller must never select for this vehicle. Example: single-phase 16 A (if the charging cable is limited to 15 A) or three-phase 6 A (if 3-phase charging should only start at 8 A).

vehicle_select.title: Edit vehicle
vehicle_select.description: Select the vehicle profile whose measured charging powers and stages you want to edit.

data_description.profile: Vehicle profile to edit. Example: Standard vehicle.

vehicle_delete.title: Delete vehicle
vehicle_delete.description: Select the vehicle profile you want to delete. The currently active vehicle or the last remaining profile cannot be deleted.

error.name_duplicate: A vehicle with this name already exists.
error.power_invalid: Every charging power must be greater than 0 W and within the allowed range.
error.power_not_increasing: Charging power must not decrease with increasing current.
error.stage_conflict: A stage cannot be unstable and excluded at the same time.
error.no_usable_stage: At least one stage must remain usable.
error.last_profile: The last vehicle profile cannot be deleted.
